label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

findings.problem: The cookie banner Deny and Allow buttons are at the very end of the keyboard order, so pressing Tab from the top never reaches them. I only found them by pressing Shift+Tab from the top to wrap to the end.

After the cookie banner was dismissed, an empty-looking [name] Policy block with no role stayed in the tab order as the first stop and had to be tabbed past on every page. The first Tab stop before it is also a link with no name.

A sign-up modal (create an account, email, Facebook and Apple sign-up) was in the page and grabbed keyboard focus; its Close modal button had no visible text name, only the label showing Close modal, and I had to close it before doing anything else.

There is no skip link to the main content. Every top menu item (New, [name], Men, Denim, Sale, Gift shop) exposes a whole mega menu of dozens of links to the keyboard, some repeated twice and several with no name, so reaching the first product needs well over 100 Tab presses. After 20 Tab presses I was still only at the first menu.

Going backwards from the end does not help: the footer has about 35 links, then pagination (Last, 1 to 7, Next) and 48 Add to bag buttons, plus many links with no accessible name. I ran out of reasonable steps before reaching any product, so I could not add anything to the bag or reach checkout.
